goal.en: Talk about salary politely: give a researched number and ask if there is room to negotiate.
goal.zh: 得體地談薪水：說出有根據的數字，並詢問是否有協商空間。

background: bright conference room with a round wooden table, a closed folder, two coffee cups and a water jug, warm pendant lights, glass wall overlooking harbor rooftops, morning

intro.en: One week later: the second interview. This time, Rachel joins Ms. Wong at the table.
intro.zh: 一週後，第二次面試。這次瑞秋也和王經理一起坐在桌邊。

intro.en: After twenty minutes of questions, Rachel opens a folder. You know what topic comes next.
intro.zh: 問了二十分鐘之後，瑞秋打開一個資料夾。你知道接下來要談什麼了。

lines.en: So, Kai, what kind of salary are you expecting for this role?
lines.zh: 那麼，凱，你對這個職位的期望薪資是多少？

choices.en: Whatever you give me is fine. I don't really dare to talk about money.
choices.zh: 你們給多少都可以，我不太敢談錢。

lines.en: Hmm. It really helps us to have a number, Kai.
lines.zh: 嗯，凱，你給我們一個數字會比較好處理。

story.en: Rachel writes down the lowest number in the range. You were polite, and it cost you a few thousand a year.
story.zh: 瑞秋寫下薪資範圍裡最低的數字。你很客氣，代價是一年少了好幾千塊。

fail.why: 在台灣談錢常被認為傷感情，但在這裡，被問期望薪資時給出有根據的數字是正常的。說 Based on my research, around 50,000 a year seems fair.。

choices.en: As much as possible! Rent in Maple Bay is crazy, you know.
choices.zh: 越多越好！楓灣的房租很誇張，你知道的。

lines.en: We all know rent is high. But we need a realistic number.
lines.zh: 大家都知道房租很高，但我們需要一個實際的數字。

story.en: Ms. Wong and Rachel share a look. Salary is about the value of the job, not about your landlord.
story.zh: 王經理和瑞秋交換了一個眼神。薪水看的是這份工作的價值，不是你的房東。

fail.why: 用「越多越好」和抱怨房租來談薪水，聽起來既不專業又像在討價還價。用市場行情當根據：Based on my research, around 50,000 a year seems fair.。

choices.en: Based on my research, around 50,000 a year seems fair.
choices.zh: 根據我查的資料，年薪五萬左右應該合理。
choices.tip: Based on my research... 讓你的數字有根據，聽起來專業而不貪心。

lines.en: Thank you. Our range for this position is 45,000 to 48,000 a year.
lines.zh: 謝謝。這個職位的薪資範圍是年薪四萬五到四萬八。

choices.en: That's too low. Other companies pay way more than that.
choices.zh: 太低了吧。其他公司給得多很多。

lines.en: Then maybe one of those companies is a better fit for you.
lines.zh: 那也許那些公司比較適合你。

story.en: The room goes quiet. Rachel slowly closes her folder, and you realize the negotiation is over.
story.zh: 會議室安靜下來。瑞秋慢慢闔上資料夾，你這才發現談判已經結束了。

fail.why: 直接說「太低了」又拿別家公司比，聽起來像在威脅。禮貌地探問空間：I understand. Is there any room for flexibility on that?。

choices.en: Hmm. Could you add a little more? Please give me some face.
choices.zh: 嗯，可以再加一點嗎？請給我點面子。

lines.en: Give you... some face? I'm not sure what you're asking for.
lines.zh: 給你……一些臉？我不太懂你要什麼。

story.en: Rachel actually looks at your face, then at Ms. Wong. Nobody is sure what to offer.
story.zh: 瑞秋真的看了看你的臉，又看向王經理。沒有人知道該給你什麼。

fail.why: 「給我面子」直譯成 give me face，英文聽不懂，而且談薪水靠的是理由，不是人情。說 Is there any room for flexibility on that?。

choices.en: I understand. Is there any room for flexibility on that?
choices.zh: 我了解。這個部分有沒有彈性空間？
choices.tip: Is there any room for flexibility? 禮貌地詢問能不能再談，不會讓氣氛變僵。

lines.en: There might be a little room. What number did you have in mind?
lines.zh: 可能有一點空間。你心裡想的數字是多少？

choices.en: I hope you can giving me 48,000, if it's possible.
choices.zh: 如果可能的話，我希望你們能給我四萬八。

lines.en: Can giving...? So, 48,000? Or are you asking?
lines.zh: Can giving……？所以是四萬八？還是你在問我們？

story.en: The sentence sounds so unsure that Ms. Wong offers 46,000 instead. Grammar, it turns out, can cost money.
story.zh: 這句話聽起來太沒把握，王經理改開了四萬六。原來文法也會影響薪水。

fail.why: can 後面接原形動詞：I hope you can give me...。談數字時語氣要穩，用問句提出：Would 48,000 work?。

choices.en: Would 48,000 work? I'm flexible on the start date.
choices.zh: 四萬八可以嗎？到職日我可以配合。
choices.tip: Would... work? 提出數字，再用 I'm flexible on... 釋出善意，雙方都有台階下。

choices.en: 48,000? Or 46,000 is also okay. Or 45,000, no problem!
choices.zh: 四萬八？還是四萬六也可以。四萬五也沒問題！

lines.en: Wait... did you just lower your own number twice?
lines.zh: 等等……你剛剛自己降價兩次？

story.en: Rachel happily writes down 45,000. You negotiated against yourself, and you won... for them.
story.zh: 瑞秋開心地寫下四萬五。你跟自己討價還價，而且贏了……替他們贏的。

fail.why: 怕對方不高興而自己先降價，在談判中等於直接讓步。提出一個數字後就停下來，等對方回應：Would 48,000 work?。

lines.en: We can work with 48,000. The role also includes health insurance and ten vacation days.
lines.zh: 四萬八我們可以接受。這個職位還有健康保險和十天年假。

choices.en: Only ten days? That's it? Well, fine, I guess I can live with that.
choices.zh: 只有十天？就這樣？好吧，我想我還能忍。

lines.en: Ten days is pretty standard here, Kai.
lines.zh: 凱，十天在這裡算是很標準的。

story.en: You just got a raise in the same meeting, and you still sound unhappy. Ms. Wong raises one eyebrow.
story.zh: 同一場會議裡才剛幫你加了薪，你聽起來還是不滿意。王經理挑起了一邊眉毛。

fail.why: 剛談好薪水就抱怨福利，會讓對方覺得怎麼給都不夠。想多爭取，換成正面的問法：Is there room for training, like a sales course?。

choices.en: Sounds great. Is there room for training, like a sales course?
choices.zh: 聽起來很好。有沒有機會參加培訓，例如業務課程？
choices.tip: Is there room for + 名詞？可以禮貌地爭取薪水以外的東西，例如培訓。

choices.en: Sound good. Ten vacation days is including holidays or not?
choices.zh: 聽起來不錯。十天年假有包含國定假日嗎？

lines.en: Is including...? Sorry, do you mean, are holidays included?
lines.zh: Is including……？抱歉，你是說有沒有包含國定假日嗎？

story.en: Rachel explains the holiday rules three times. The meeting runs ten minutes over, all because of one tangled question.
story.zh: 瑞秋把放假規定解釋了三遍。會議因為一個打結的問題，超時了十分鐘。

fail.why: 英文問句要把 be 動詞放前面，「包含」用被動 included：Are holidays included?。另外主詞是 It 時要說 Sounds good，不是 Sound good。

lines.en: We can look into a course. We'll make our final decision this week.
lines.zh: 課程的部分我們可以研究看看。這週內我們會做最後決定。

choices.en: Please decide fast. Another company wants me too, you know.
choices.zh: 請快點決定，你知道的，也有其他公司想要我。

lines.en: Then I hope you'll make the right choice, whatever it is.
lines.zh: 那希望你做出正確的選擇，不管是哪一個。

story.en: There is no other company. Ms. Wong doesn't know that, but she doesn't seem worried either.
story.zh: 其實根本沒有其他公司。王經理不知道這件事，但她看起來也一點都不擔心。

fail.why: 用別家公司施壓，會讓人覺得你在耍手段，也破壞剛建立的好感。用感謝和期待收尾：Thank you both. I'm really excited about this opportunity.。

choices.en: Thank you both. You have worked very hard today!
choices.zh: 謝謝兩位，你們今天辛苦了！

lines.en: Um... thanks? It was just one meeting, but okay.
lines.zh: 呃……謝謝？只是開了一場會，不過好吧。

story.en: Rachel bites her lip to stop laughing. It feels like you just gave your future boss a performance review.
story.zh: 瑞秋咬著嘴唇忍住笑。感覺像你剛幫未來的老闆打了考績。

fail.why: 「辛苦了」直譯成 You worked very hard，英文聽起來像在評價對方的表現。結束時說 Thank you for your time. 或 I'm really excited about this opportunity. 就好。

choices.en: Thank you both. I'm really excited about this opportunity.
choices.zh: 謝謝兩位，我對這個機會真的很期待。
choices.tip: 談完條件後用 I'm excited about this opportunity. 收尾，提醒對方你很有誠意。

lines.en: So are we, Kai. It was a pleasure.
lines.zh: 我們也是，凱。很高興和你談。

lines.en: You'll hear from us very soon.
lines.zh: 你很快就會收到我們的消息。

story.en: You asked for a fair number, stayed polite and even got a course on the table. Not bad for your first negotiation in English.
story.zh: 你提出合理的數字、保持禮貌，還爭取到了課程。第一次用英文談判，表現得很不錯。

notes.en: Based on my research, ... seems fair.
notes.zh: 根據我查的資料，……應該合理。
notes.explain: 被問期望薪資時，用市場行情當根據，給出一個數字或範圍，不要說「隨便」。

example.en: Based on my research, 48,000 to 50,000 seems fair for this role.
example.zh: 根據我查的資料，這個職位四萬八到五萬應該合理。

notes.explain: room 在這裡是「空間、餘地」。Is there any room for flexibility? 問薪水能不能談；Is there room for training? 問有沒有培訓機會。

example.en: Is there any room for growth in this role?
example.zh: 這個職位有成長空間嗎？

notes.explain: 談判時在一件事上讓步，換取另一件事。這比中文直譯的 I can cooperate 自然得多。

example.en: I'm flexible on the start date, but I'd like a training course.
example.zh: 到職日我可以配合，但我希望能上培訓課程。

notes.en: give me face / You worked hard today
notes.explain: 這兩句直譯英文都很怪。談條件靠理由，不靠面子；道別時說 Thank you for your time.，不要說 You worked hard.。

example.en: Thank you for your time. I really appreciate it.
example.zh: 謝謝你撥空，真的很感謝。

notes.explain: 在許多英語系國家，禮貌地談薪水很常見，不會傷感情。提出數字後就停下來等對方回應，不要自己先降價，也不要用別家公司施壓。

example.zh: 四萬八你們可以接受嗎？
